h1sr: Quantum Lab: will crypto survive a quantum computer?
lead: Every crypto wallet proves "this is really me" with a digital signature. A big enough quantum computer could one day fake today's signatures. New quantum-safe signatures already exist. Try both below: this is real cryptography, running only in your browser.
edWho: The signature Solana uses now (also many other blockchains).
mlWho: Official US standard since August 2024 (NIST FIPS 204).
faWho: Smaller signatures. The one Solana developers picked for their quantum plan (2026).
qP: What if a big quantum computer existed? Switch one on in the simulation and see which signatures still hold.
honest: Honest note: the keys and signatures above are real and made on your device; nothing is sent anywhere and you can't use them for a wallet. The quantum computer is a simulation: nobody can break Ed25519 today.
howH: The quantum problem in four steps
w1p: Your wallet has a secret key and a public key. Only the secret key can sign; everyone can check with the public key.
w2p: Going from the public key back to the secret key would take normal computers longer than the age of the universe.
w3p: A large quantum computer running Shor's algorithm could do it. Such a machine does not exist yet; experts disagree on when it will.
w4p: Post-quantum signatures like ML-DSA and Falcon use problems quantum computers can't shortcut. They are bigger, but they work.
m1p: No. AI can help find bugs in code, but it is not a lock. Safety comes from proven math (like the standards in this lab) and careful audits. Be careful with any project that says "secured by AI".
m2: "We need a quantum computer to stay safe from quantum computers."
m2p: No. Quantum-safe signatures run on normal phones and laptops, as you just saw. Quantum key distribution exists too, but it needs special hardware and doesn't help a blockchain.
m3p: Not tomorrow. Today's quantum computers are far too small. But blockchains move slowly, so big networks like Solana are preparing now.
m4p: Not yet, just like every Solana token today. $MAIGA lives on Solana, so it gets quantum safety when Solana upgrades its signatures. We will not claim more than that. Entertainment only. NFA. DYOR.
checked: Facts checked October 2026: NIST published FIPS 203, 204 and 205 in August 2024; Falcon is being standardised as FN-DSA; Solana developers announced Falcon as their post-quantum signature in 2026.
ctaP: Want to see how a blockchain works first? Build your own mini blockchain in the browser, block by block.
